emt-exam-l01.q: You are 95 questions into the cognitive exam and it is still going. What does that tell you?
choices: You are failing, because passing candidates always shut off at 70
The computer has not yet reached 95% confidence either way, which says nothing about pass or fail
You have already passed and the rest are pilot items
The exam has switched to the pediatric section
emt-exam-l01.why: The exam runs between 70 and 120 items and stops when the computer is 95% confident your ability is above or below the standard. A long exam means the estimate is still near the line, not that you failed.

emt-exam-l01.q: Your exam fee, authorization to test letter and scheduling all run through which combination?
choices: Your state EMS office, which mails the ATT and schedules you
Your course instructor, who registers you directly at a testing center
The National Registry issues the ATT after course-completion verification, and you schedule at Pearson VUE
Pearson VUE issues the ATT and the National Registry schedules the seat
emt-exam-l01.why: Your course director verifies completion, the National Registry issues the Authorization to Test with an eligibility window, and you book the seat yourself at a Pearson VUE center.

emt-exam-l02.q: A stem describes a 60-year-old with chest pain, gives you a full set of vitals and a clear airway, then asks for the BEST action. Two choices are reasonable. What does the cue word BEST tell you?
choices: Pick the fastest of the reasonable options
Pick the cheapest option that does no harm
Pick the one your local protocol allows
Several choices are acceptable, so pick the one representing the highest standard of care
emt-exam-l02.why: BEST and MOST APPROPRIATE signal that more than one choice works. The test wants the highest standard of care, not the quickest or the most local option.

emt-exam-l02.q: A stem says a patient's wife hands you her own prescribed nitroglycerin for her husband's chest pain. What kind of distractor is 'assist him with his wife's nitroglycerin'?
choices: A correct action, since nitroglycerin is nitroglycerin
Something that sounds authoritative but is outside your authority, because the drug is not prescribed to this patient
A timing error only, correct after vitals
A scope question that depends on your county protocol
emt-exam-l02.why: EMTs assist only with medications prescribed to that patient. A drug belonging to a family member is never the answer regardless of how well the symptoms fit.

emt-exam-l03.q: During scene size-up you count four patients and you have one ambulance. When do you request additional units?
choices: After completing the primary survey on the sickest patient
After baseline vitals on all four
During size-up, before you commit to any single patient
Only after the first patient is packaged
emt-exam-l03.why: Requesting resources is part of scene size-up. Once you are kneeling next to one patient nobody is counting the rest, so the call goes out before you commit.

emt-exam-l03.q: An adult collapses in front of you, is unresponsive, not breathing, and has no pulse. Which sequence is correct?
choices: Compressions, then airway, then breathing
Airway, then breathing, then compressions
Two rescue breaths, then compressions
Open the airway, insert an OPA, then check a pulse again
emt-exam-l03.why: Adult arrest is CAB. The blood is still oxygenated at the moment of collapse and the problem is that nothing is moving it, so compressions lead. Newborns are the reverse, because their arrest is a breathing problem.

emt-exam-l04.q: You are sizing a nasopharyngeal airway for an adult. Which measurement is correct?
choices: Corner of the mouth to the earlobe
Nostril to the angle of the jaw on the opposite side
Nostril to the earlobe
Nose tip to the sternal notch
emt-exam-l04.why: NPA sizing runs from the nostril to the earlobe; corner-of-the-mouth to earlobe is the OPA measurement. Mixing them up is one of the most common airway errors.

emt-exam-l04.q: A 68-year-old with chest pain has a systolic of 132 and took no erectile dysfunction medication. He has already had two nitroglycerin doses five minutes apart and still hurts. What is correct?
choices: One more dose is permitted, for a maximum of three total, five minutes after the second
No further doses; two is the maximum
Give two more doses back to back to get ahead of the pain
Switch to aspirin 324 mg only after four nitroglycerin doses
emt-exam-l04.why: Nitroglycerin is 0.4 mg sublingual every 5 minutes up to 3 doses with a systolic above 100. He has had two and qualifies for one more; stacking doses or exceeding three is wrong.

emt-exam-l05.q: A 22 kg child in anaphylaxis needs epinephrine. What dose applies?
choices: 0.3 mg intramuscular, because any child in anaphylaxis gets the adult dose
0.5 mg intramuscular
0.15 mg intramuscular, the pediatric auto-injector dose for 15 to 30 kg
0.1 mg subcutaneous
emt-exam-l05.why: The pediatric auto-injector delivers 0.15 mg and covers roughly 15 to 30 kg. A 22 kg child falls inside that band; the 0.3 mg adult dose is for patients above about 30 kg.

emt-exam-l05.q: A 30-week pregnant patient with a headache has a blood pressure of 158/98 and swelling of her hands and face. She has not had a seizure. What is this?
choices: Preeclampsia, defined as 140/90 or higher after 20 weeks with headache, vision changes or edema
Eclampsia, because the pressure is that high
Placental abruption
Normal late-pregnancy physiology
emt-exam-l05.why: Preeclampsia is 140/90 or higher after 20 weeks with symptoms such as headache, vision changes and edema. It becomes eclampsia only when a seizure occurs; abruption is painful dark bleeding with a rigid uterus.

emt-exam-l06.q: You are applying a tourniquet to a mid-calf wound that direct pressure has not controlled. Where does it go?
choices: Directly over the wound so pressure is focused
At the knee joint, the nearest bony landmark
2 to 3 inches above the wound, not over a joint, tightened until bleeding stops
As high on the thigh as possible in every case
emt-exam-l06.why: A tourniquet goes 2 to 3 inches proximal to the wound and never over a joint, because a joint prevents even compression of the vessel. It is tightened until bleeding stops and the time is written down.

emt-exam-l06.q: A child has burns to the entire head and the entire front of the torso. Using the pediatric rule of nines, what percentage is burned?
emt-exam-l06.why: In a child the head counts 18% rather than the adult 9%, and the front torso is 18%, giving 36%. Using the adult head value of 9% produces the tempting 27% answer.

emt-exam-l07.q: During the bag-valve-mask station, you stop ventilating for 40 seconds to reposition the oxygen tubing. What happens?
choices: Nothing, as long as ventilation resumes
Points are deducted but the station continues
The station is failed, because interrupting ventilation for more than 30 seconds is a critical criterion
The evaluator restarts the clock
emt-exam-l07.why: Interrupting ventilation for more than 30 seconds is on the critical criteria list and ends the station regardless of how well the rest went.

emt-exam-l07.q: A patient has an angulated, painful elbow with a strong radial pulse. At the joint immobilization station, what is correct?
choices: Straighten the joint gently, then splint
Splint the joint as found, immobilizing the bone above and below, and reassess distal pulse, motor and sensation
Apply traction until alignment is restored
Splint only the forearm, since the pulse is present
emt-exam-l07.why: An injured joint with a pulse present is splinted as found. Joint immobilization secures the bone above and below the joint, and distal pulse, motor and sensation are checked before and after.

emt-exam-l08.q: Of the 40 NCCP hours required for EMT recertification, how many are individual hours you choose yourself?
choices: 0, all hours are specified
emt-exam-l08.why: The NCCP split for EMT is 20 national hours, 10 local or state hours, and 10 individual hours you select, often your weakest domains.

emt-exam-l08.q: Which step is required for New Jersey EMT certification but is not part of the National Registry process?
choices: Passing a cognitive exam
Holding a current healthcare-provider BLS card
Completing an approved EMT course
A criminal history background check with fingerprinting through NJ OEMS
emt-exam-l08.why: The NJ OEMS application adds a fingerprinted criminal history background check and a state fee. The course, the CPR card and the cognitive exam sit on the national side of the process.

emt-exam-l09.q: It is week one of your four-week plan. What do you do before studying anything?
choices: Reread the airway chapter, since airway is the most tested
Build flashcards for every number in the textbook
Take a 50-question mixed set cold and score it by domain to build your syllabus
Take a full 120-question timed exam to simulate the real thing
emt-exam-l09.why: The cold 50-question baseline tells you where you actually are by domain, and that profile becomes your study plan. Full-length simulations belong in week four, after the content work.

emt-exam-l09.q: Which item in your bag will get you turned away at the Pearson VUE center?
choices: Nothing, as long as valuables go in the locker
A second non-photo form of identification
A wallet
Nothing at all, because personal items are simply stored
emt-exam-l09.why: Phones, watches, food and notes all go into a locker before you enter, so carrying them is not itself disqualifying. What does end the attempt is arriving late or lacking a government photo ID with your signature matching your registry account.

emt-exam-l10.q: A D cylinder reads 1,000 psi and you are running 15 L/min by nonrebreather. About how many minutes of oxygen remain before the 200 psi residual?
choices: About 21 minutes
About 8.5 minutes
About 15 minutes
About 30 minutes
emt-exam-l10.why: Using (psi minus 200) times the constant divided by flow: (1000 - 200) x 0.16 / 15 equals about 8.5 minutes. Forgetting the 200 psi residual or using the E constant of 0.28 produces the longer, wrong answers.

emt-exam-l10.q: A patient on CPAP for pulmonary edema becomes drowsy, stops following commands, and his systolic falls from 160 to 88. You should:
choices: Increase the CPAP pressure above 10 cmH2O
Leave CPAP in place and continue transport
Remove CPAP and assist ventilations with a bag-valve mask
Remove CPAP and apply a nonrebreather at 15 L/min
emt-exam-l10.why: Drowsiness, loss of command-following and a falling pressure are all CPAP stop signs. A patient who can no longer protect his airway or maintain pressure needs assisted ventilation, not more pressure and not a passive mask.

emt-exam-l11.q: During adult CPR, what compression fraction should you maintain and how long may an interruption last?
choices: Above 60% fraction, interruptions under 10 seconds
Above 40% fraction, interruptions under 30 seconds
Above 80% fraction, interruptions under 5 seconds
Fraction does not matter as long as the rate is 100 to 120
emt-exam-l11.why: The target is a compression fraction above 60% with interruptions held under 10 seconds. Rate and depth matter, but hands-off time is what actually drops coronary perfusion pressure.

emt-exam-l11.q: A STEMI pattern in leads II, III and aVF with hypotension and clear lungs should make you:
choices: Give nitroglycerin, since the systolic will rise once pain is treated
Withhold nitroglycerin because of a possible right ventricular infarct
Withhold aspirin
Assume the 12-lead is artifact
emt-exam-l11.why: II, III and aVF is an inferior pattern, and inferior infarct with hypotension and clear lungs suggests right ventricular involvement, which is preload-dependent. Nitroglycerin drops preload and can crash the pressure; aspirin is still indicated.

emt-exam-l12.q: An adult trauma patient has lost roughly 25% of his blood volume. What do you expect to see?
choices: A systolic under 90 with a slow heart rate
Normal vitals throughout
Tachycardia with a still-normal blood pressure
Warm, dry, flushed skin
emt-exam-l12.why: Loss of 15 to 30% produces compensated shock: tachycardia, anxiety, delayed capillary refill, and a pressure that is still normal. The pressure falls only above about 30% loss.

emt-exam-l12.q: You cut the clothing off a trauma patient in a cold ambulance in order to examine him. What must follow immediately?
choices: Nothing; exposure is the goal and cooling is protective
Apply cold packs to any deformities
Open the windows to keep the crew alert
Cover the patient and warm the compartment, because hypothermia is one leg of the trauma triad of death
emt-exam-l12.why: The trauma triad of death is hypothermia, acidosis and coagulopathy. Leaving a trauma patient exposed actively worsens bleeding by impairing clotting, so expose, examine, then cover and warm.

emt-exam-l13.q: A patient has been seizing continuously for 7 minutes. What does this mean?
choices: A normal seizure that should be allowed to finish
Status epilepticus, an ALS emergency
A pseudoseizure, since real seizures stop in 2 minutes
A febrile seizure by definition
emt-exam-l13.why: Five minutes of continuous seizing, or repeated seizures without regaining consciousness between them, defines status epilepticus. It needs ALS for a benzodiazepine, not patience.

emt-exam-l13.q: A stroke patient's last known well time was 90 minutes ago. Why does that number matter more than the stroke scale score?
choices: It determines whether you give aspirin
It sets the ambulance driving speed
It decides whether clot-dissolving drugs, generally considered within 3 to 4.5 hours, are still an option
It determines the oxygen flow rate
emt-exam-l13.why: The scale identifies that a stroke is happening; the clock decides what the hospital can do about it. Clot-dissolving drugs are generally considered within 3 to 4.5 hours of last known well, and aspirin is never given for stroke.

emt-exam-l14.q: You arrive first at a multiple-casualty incident with 14 patients. How many people should any one supervisor directly manage?
choices: 3 to 7, ideally 5
1 to 2
8 to 12
As many as are available
emt-exam-l14.why: Span of control in the incident command system runs 3 to 7 subordinates with 5 as the target. More than that and a supervisor loses track of who is doing what.

emt-exam-l14.q: Medical control gives you an order over the radio. What must you do before carrying it out?
choices: Confirm it with your partner only
Repeat the order back word for word
Write it down and carry it out silently
Ask the receiving hospital to confirm it in writing
emt-exam-l14.why: Every order received over the radio is echoed back word for word so both parties catch a misheard drug or dose. Silent compliance is how wrong-dose errors happen.

emt-exam-l15.q: A stem describes a patient who improved after your intervention and asks what to do next. Which pattern is this and what is the decode?
choices: Deterioration after an intervention; undo what you did
Improvement after treatment; reassess and continue, do not escalate
Two correct actions; the cue word decides
A scope violation is hidden in the choices
emt-exam-l15.why: Improvement calls for reassessment and continued care. The mirror pattern, deterioration right after an intervention, is the one that points back at the intervention itself, and candidates routinely reverse the two.

emt-exam-l15.q: A stem gives you a patient's weight in kilograms. What should that detail warn you about?
choices: A dose, rate or ratio in the answer choices is about to change
The patient needs a bariatric stretcher
The scene is unsafe
The question is asking about transport destination
emt-exam-l15.why: A stated weight or age is put there to make a number matter: an epinephrine dose, a compression ratio, or a ventilation rate. Details in an NREMT stem are rarely decorative.

emt-exam-l16.q: In the trauma assessment station, how many times should you press the pelvis?
choices: Three times to confirm the finding
Once gently, stopping if it is unstable
Continuously while palpating the abdomen
Not at all; pelvic assessment is skipped
emt-exam-l16.why: The pelvis is compressed once, gently, and you stop immediately if it is unstable. Repeated pressing on an unstable pelvis disrupts clot and causes further bleeding, which counts as worsening patient injury.

emt-exam-l16.q: You are running the medical assessment station on a patient with chest pain. Which action costs you points?
choices: Taking an OPQRST history before the focused exam
Auscultating lung sounds and checking neck veins
Performing a full head-to-toe rapid trauma sweep instead of a focused exam
Stating your field impression and treatment plan out loud
emt-exam-l16.why: The medical station is history-driven: OPQRST, SAMPLE, then a focused exam of the relevant system. Running a trauma head-to-toe on a medical patient burns time and misses the scored components.

emt-exam-l17.q: You check the clock at question 35 and you have used 55 minutes. What does that tell you?
choices: You are on pace and should continue as you are
You are averaging about 94 seconds per item, above target, and are likely rereading rather than deciding
You should skip ahead and flag the remaining items
You should request extra time from the proctor
emt-exam-l17.why: 55 minutes over 35 items is about 94 seconds each against a 45 to 60 second target, which signals rereading. You cannot flag, skip or return to items on an adaptive exam, and no extra time is available.

emt-exam-l17.q: Which is the first step of the 20-second protocol when you blank on an item?
choices: Reread only the last line of the stem to find the cue word
Reread the entire stem from the beginning
Eliminate any out-of-scope choice
Pick the longest answer
emt-exam-l17.why: The cue word lives in the last line, so that is where you go first. Naming the patient, eliminating out-of-scope and harmful options, and falling back on the priority order come after.

quiz.q: What are the minimum and maximum number of questions on the EMT cognitive exam, and how long do you have?
choices: 70 to 120 questions in 2 hours
60 to 110 questions in 2 hours
70 to 120 questions in 2.5 hours
80 to 150 questions in 3 hours
quiz.why: The EMT cognitive exam runs 70 to 120 items with a 2-hour limit that includes any break you take. The other spans borrow numbers from the paramedic exam or from older formats and are not current.

quiz.q: A candidate has failed the cognitive exam three times. What must happen before the fourth attempt?
choices: Nothing; attempts are unlimited as long as 15 days pass between them
Completion of a documented remedial training program, after which three more attempts are allowed
The entire EMT course must be repeated immediately
A one-year waiting period with no additional training
quiz.why: After three failures the National Registry requires documented remedial training, then grants three more attempts for a maximum of six. Repeating the whole course comes only after those six are exhausted, and the 15-day wait applies between every attempt, not in place of remediation.

quiz.q: A candidate has two weeks left and has studied trauma heavily because it interests him. His baseline test shows him weakest in Medical and OB-GYN. Based on exam weighting, where should his remaining time go?
choices: Trauma, because it is the most commonly tested domain
EMS Operations, because it is pure recall
Medical and OB-GYN, which is 27 to 31% of the exam and his weakest area
Split evenly across all five domains
quiz.why: Medical and OB-GYN is the largest domain at 27 to 31% and it is also his measured weakness, so it pays twice. Trauma is 14 to 18%, the second smallest, and an even split ignores both the weighting and his own data.

quiz.q: A stem gives a complete set of vitals, a patent airway and adequate breathing on an alert patient with chest pain, then asks which action is MOST APPROPRIATE. Two choices are things you could reasonably do. How should you decide?
choices: Choose whichever action is fastest to perform
Choose the one that requires the least equipment
Choose the action your instructor said your county prefers
Choose the one representing the highest standard of care, since the cue word means several are acceptable
quiz.why: MOST APPROPRIATE and BEST signal that more than one choice is defensible and the test wants the highest standard of care. Speed, equipment and local protocol are not the deciding factors; the National Registry writes to a national standard.

quiz.q: An NREMT stem does not mention your partner, your equipment, or any scene hazard. Which set of assumptions is correct?
choices: You have a partner, a fully stocked BLS ambulance, standing orders for the EMT scope, and a safe scene
You are alone with a jump bag and must call for everything else
You have ALS on scene with you unless told otherwise
You should apply your own county protocol whenever it differs from the national standard
quiz.why: Unless the stem says otherwise, assume a partner, full BLS equipment, standing orders within the EMT scope, and a safe scene. Assuming you are alone, assuming ALS is present, or substituting local protocol all push you toward the wrong choice.

quiz.q: A 40-year-old is unresponsive with agonal gasps and a weak carotid pulse. The choices include 'request ALS', 'begin bag-valve-mask ventilation', 'apply a nonrebreather' and 'obtain a SAMPLE history'. The stem asks what you do FIRST.
choices: Request ALS, since he needs an advanced airway
Begin bag-valve-mask ventilation
Apply a nonrebreather at 15 L/min
Obtain a SAMPLE history from the family
quiz.why: Agonal gasps are inadequate breathing, so the answer is to ventilate, not to oxygenate a patient who is barely moving air. Requesting ALS is correct but never before the immediate life threat is addressed, and history-taking always loses to a breathing problem.

quiz.q: Which list correctly names the components of scene size-up?
choices: Airway, breathing, circulation, disability, exposure
Onset, provocation, quality, region, severity, time
Scene safety, standard precautions, mechanism or nature of illness, number of patients, need for additional resources
Signs, allergies, medications, past history, last intake, events
quiz.why: Scene size-up is safety, precautions, mechanism or nature of illness, patient count and resource need. The other lists are the primary survey, OPQRST and SAMPLE, all of which happen after size-up.

quiz.q: A 33-year-old has a deep groin laceration pumping bright red blood and is making snoring sounds. Which action comes first?
choices: Open the airway with a jaw thrust
Apply a nonrebreather at 15 L/min
Insert an oropharyngeal airway
Pack the wound with a hemostatic dressing and hold firm pressure
quiz.why: Massive external hemorrhage is the X in XABC and outranks the airway, because an emptied tank kills faster than a partly obstructed airway in a breathing patient. The groin is junctional, so packing with sustained pressure replaces a tourniquet, which cannot be placed there.

quiz.q: A newborn delivered 4 minutes ago is limp and apneic with a heart rate of 44 despite drying, warming and stimulation. Compared with an adult in arrest, the resuscitation sequence here is:
choices: Ventilation-led, because newborn arrest is a breathing problem, unlike the compression-first adult sequence
Identical to the adult, starting with compressions
Compression-led at 30:2
Defibrillation-led as soon as an AED arrives
quiz.why: Newborn arrest is almost always hypoxic, so effective ventilation leads and compressions are added at 3:1 only if the heart rate stays under 60 after 30 seconds of good ventilation. Adults get CAB because their circulating blood is still oxygenated, and newborns are not AED candidates.

quiz.q: You arrive to find a 70-year-old slumped in a chair with gurgling respirations. Your partner begins asking the daughter about medications. The stem asks for your priority.
choices: Complete the SAMPLE history so you know what he takes
Suction the airway
Obtain a full set of baseline vitals
Apply the AED pads
quiz.why: Gurgling means fluid in the airway and the fix is suction, performed the moment you find it rather than after finishing an assessment list. History and vitals belong after the primary survey, and AED pads are for a pulseless patient.

quiz.q: Which oxygen device and flow combination is correct?
choices: Nasal cannula at 10 to 15 L/min
Nonrebreather at 4 to 6 L/min
Nasal cannula at 1 to 6 L/min, delivering 24 to 44%
Bag-valve mask with reservoir at 6 L/min
quiz.why: A cannula runs 1 to 6 L/min for 24 to 44% oxygen. Running a cannula at 15 L/min dries the nose without adding much oxygen, a nonrebreather needs 10 to 15 L/min to keep the reservoir full, and a BVM reservoir needs 15 L/min to approach 100%.

quiz.q: You are inserting an oropharyngeal airway in a 5-year-old with no gag reflex. The correct technique is:
choices: Insert upside down and rotate 180 degrees, as in an adult
Insert sideways and rotate 90 degrees
Insert through the nose after lubricating it
Insert right side up using a tongue depressor to hold the tongue down
quiz.why: Children get the OPA inserted right side up with a tongue blade, because rotating a rigid airway against a child's soft palate and tissues causes bleeding. The 180-degree rotation is the adult technique, and nasal insertion describes an NPA.

quiz.q: A 60-year-old with chest pain has a systolic of 112 and has already taken his own nitroglycerin twice at home, 20 minutes apart. He takes no PDE-5 inhibitor. What is appropriate?
choices: You may assist with one more dose, to a maximum of three total, 5 minutes after the last
No more nitroglycerin; his home doses do not count toward the maximum
Give two more doses immediately since the interval has already passed
Withhold nitroglycerin because the systolic is under 120
quiz.why: The three-dose maximum counts every dose including the ones the patient took himself, so he qualifies for one more with a systolic above 100. Home doses absolutely count, stacking doses is unsafe, and 100 is the systolic threshold, not 120.

quiz.q: A 74-year-old has swollen ankles, distended neck veins, an enlarged tender liver, and clear lung sounds. This picture points to:
choices: Left-sided heart failure with pulmonary edema
Right-sided heart failure, which backs fluid into the body rather than the lungs
Cardiogenic shock
A massive pulmonary embolism
quiz.why: Right-sided failure backs fluid up into the systemic circulation: pedal edema, distended neck veins and hepatomegaly with clear lungs. Left-sided failure would give crackles and pink frothy sputum, cardiogenic shock adds hypotension, and a PE presents with sudden dyspnea and hypoxia that resists oxygen.

quiz.q: A 6-year-old struck by a car has a blood pressure of 76/50. Applying the minimum-systolic formula for children 1 to 10 years, this pressure is:
choices: Normal for age
Above the minimum, so shock is unlikely
Below the minimum of 82, indicating decompensated shock
Not interpretable without a weight
quiz.why: Minimum acceptable systolic for ages 1 to 10 is 70 plus twice the age, so 70 plus 12 equals 82. At 76 this child is below that floor, and because children compensate hard before dropping pressure, a low number means late, decompensated shock.

quiz.q: A 33-week pregnant patient has painless, bright red vaginal bleeding with a soft, non-tender uterus and no trauma history. You should suspect:
choices: Placental abruption
Ectopic pregnancy
Uterine rupture
Placenta previa
quiz.why: Previa is painless bright red bleeding with a soft uterus. Abruption is painful dark bleeding with a rigid tender uterus, ectopic pregnancy occurs in the first trimester, and uterine rupture presents with severe pain and shock.

quiz.q: A 28-week pregnant patient is supine on your stretcher and becomes lightheaded with a falling blood pressure. Your first action is:
choices: Tilt or roll her onto her left side
Sit her fully upright
Place her in Trendelenburg
Apply a nonrebreather and continue supine
quiz.why: After 20 weeks the uterus compresses the vena cava when the patient is supine, cutting venous return. Left lateral tilt takes the weight off the vessel immediately; oxygen and head-down positioning do not fix the mechanical obstruction.

quiz.q: A 19-year-old drank a large amount of drain cleaner 10 minutes ago. He is alert with an intact gag reflex and burns around his lips. Your protocol carries activated charcoal. You should:
choices: Give activated charcoal 1 g/kg since the gag reflex is intact and the ingestion is recent
Withhold charcoal, because it is contraindicated for caustics, and manage the airway with rapid transport
Induce vomiting before transport
Give oral water to dilute the caustic
quiz.why: Activated charcoal does not bind caustics and vomiting it back up burns the esophagus a second time. Induced vomiting is contraindicated for the same reason, and forcing fluids risks aspiration in a patient whose airway may swell.

quiz.q: A 45-year-old has heavy bleeding from a wound just below the left knee. Direct pressure with two dressings has failed. A tourniquet should be placed:
choices: Directly over the wound
Across the knee joint
On the thigh, 2 to 3 inches above the wound and clear of the joint
On the ankle, below the wound
quiz.why: A tourniquet goes 2 to 3 inches proximal to the wound and never across a joint, because a joint prevents even vessel compression. Placing it over the wound or distal to it does nothing to stop arterial inflow.

quiz.q: An EMT skipped a spinal assessment on a patient who had midline neck tenderness. The patient had no neurologic injury and suffered no harm, but files a complaint. Regarding negligence:
choices: Negligence is established because the standard of care was breached
Negligence is established because a duty to act existed
Negligence depends only on whether the EMT intended harm
Negligence is not established, because all four elements including actual damages must be present
quiz.why: Negligence requires duty, breach, causation and damages, all four. A breach without resulting harm fails the damages element, and intent is irrelevant to negligence, which is a failure-of-care standard rather than a deliberate act.

quiz.q: A 3-year-old has burns to the entire head and both entire arms. Using the pediatric rule of nines, the burned surface area is:
quiz.why: In a child the head is 18% rather than the adult 9%, and each arm remains 9%, giving 18 plus 9 plus 9 equals 36%. Using the adult head value produces the tempting 27% answer, which is the error the item is built around.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a critical criterion that fails a psychomotor skill station outright?
choices: Taking 11 minutes on a 10-minute assessment station
Failing to verbalize standard precautions at the start of the station
Asking the evaluator to repeat a vital sign
Applying a cervical collar before auscultating the chest
quiz.why: Failing to take or verbalize standard precautions is on the critical criteria list and ends the station regardless of performance. Timing, clarifying questions and reasonable sequence variations are scored normally, not as instant failures.

quiz.q: At the long bone immobilization station you splint a mid-shaft tibia fracture. Which action is required both before and after splinting?
choices: Application of a traction splint
Auscultation of lung sounds
Assessment of distal pulse, motor function and sensation
Measurement of a blood pressure in the injured limb
quiz.why: Distal pulse, motor and sensation are checked before and after splinting, and failing to do so is a critical criterion. A traction splint is for mid-shaft femur, not tibia, and lung sounds and limb pressures are not part of this station.

quiz.q: A candidate hears that the National Registry no longer requires a separate psychomotor exam for EMT and concludes the skills standard has been relaxed. What is accurate as of 2026?
choices: The standard was lowered because evaluators are no longer involved
The skill sheets were retired along with the exam
The change applies nationwide on a single date, so no state uses the old model
Skills verification moved into the approved course, the same skill sheets and critical criteria apply, and states are on different timelines
quiz.why: Verification shifted from a separate state-coordinated exam into the approved course, but the sheets and the critical criteria are unchanged. States implement on different timelines, so both models are alive as of 2026 and your course director tells you which applies.

quiz.q: Under the National Continued Competency Program, how are the 40 EMT recertification hours divided?
choices: 20 national, 10 local or state, 10 individual
10 national, 20 local or state, 10 individual
20 national, 20 individual, 0 local
40 hours chosen entirely by the candidate
quiz.why: The NCCP split for EMT is 20 national, 10 local or state and 10 individual hours. The national hours are the most specific and hardest to find late, which is why the other splits are attractive but wrong.

quiz.q: You passed the National Registry cognitive exam last week and a New Jersey hospital wants to hire you as an emergency department technician. What is the realistic next step?
choices: You may work immediately anywhere in New Jersey on the National Registry card alone
Apply to NJ OEMS for state certification including the fee and a fingerprinted background check, while asking whether the employer will hire pending the state card
Wait for the state card before applying to any job, since employment before it is issued is prohibited
Request that NJ OEMS waive the background check because the Registry already screened you
quiz.why: New Jersey certification is a separate application with a fee and a fingerprinted criminal history check, and processing takes weeks. Many New Jersey hospitals hire EMTs on the Registry card while the state card processes, so the right move is to apply immediately and ask rather than assume.

quiz.q: An EMT completes his National Registry recertification in March and assumes his New Jersey certification is now current as well. What is the problem with that assumption?
choices: There is no problem; the Registry reports hours to the state automatically
New Jersey certification never expires once issued
The two credentials run on separate cycles with separate continuing-education requirements and must be tracked independently
The Registry certification is the only one an employer requires
quiz.why: National and state certifications are two cards on two clocks: the Registry uses a 2-year NCCP cycle, and New Jersey runs its own renewal cycle and CE requirement, currently three years. Employers want copies of both plus a current CPR card, and hours are not transferred automatically.

quiz.q: A candidate studies by rereading his textbook chapters twice and highlighting. He feels well prepared but scores poorly on practice sets. The most likely explanation is:
choices: He needs a third pass through the book
The practice questions are harder than the real exam
He needs more sleep before practice sets
Rereading builds familiarity, which feels like knowledge, while only retrieval practice builds durable recall
quiz.why: Familiarity from rereading is not the same as being able to retrieve an answer cold, which is exactly what the exam tests. The fix is question-first study and spaced retrieval, not another pass through the text.

quiz.q: What belongs in an error log entry after you miss a practice question?
choices: The topic, why you missed it, and the correct rule
Only the question number, for later review
The full text of the question and all four choices
A tally of how many you missed that day
quiz.why: One line per miss with topic, cause and rule is what makes the log reviewable weekly. Copying full questions makes the log too long to reread, and a bare tally records the score without capturing the pattern behind it.

quiz.q: You arrive at the testing center with your driver's license and a credit card bearing your signature. Your Registry account lists your full middle name but your license shows only a middle initial. What is the risk?
choices: None, as long as you have two forms of identification
Names that do not match the registry account exactly can cost you the seat, so the mismatch must be resolved before exam day
The credit card is not acceptable under any circumstances
You will simply be assigned a later testing slot
quiz.why: The requirement is two forms of identification, one a government photo ID with your signature, with names matching your Registry account exactly. A mismatch is worth fixing in advance, and forfeiting the fee is a real outcome rather than a rescheduling.

quiz.q: An E cylinder reads 1,200 psi and your patient is on a nonrebreather at 15 L/min. Approximately how long until the cylinder reaches the 200 psi residual?
choices: About 22 minutes
About 11 minutes
About 19 minutes
About 33 minutes
quiz.why: Using (psi minus 200) times the constant divided by flow: (1200 - 200) x 0.28 / 15 is about 18.7 minutes. Forgetting the 200 psi residual gives roughly 22 minutes, and using the D constant of 0.16 gives about 11.

quiz.q: Which set of values is correct for a healthy adult?
choices: Respiratory rate 20 to 30, tidal volume 1,000 mL, ETCO2 25 to 35 mmHg
Respiratory rate 12 to 20, tidal volume about 500 mL, ETCO2 55 to 65 mmHg
Respiratory rate 8 to 12, tidal volume about 250 mL, ETCO2 35 to 45 mmHg
Respiratory rate 12 to 20, tidal volume about 500 mL, ETCO2 35 to 45 mmHg
quiz.why: Adults breathe 12 to 20 times per minute at roughly 500 mL per breath with an ETCO2 of 35 to 45 mmHg. The other sets move one value out of range each, and an ETCO2 of 55 to 65 would indicate hypoventilation rather than normal physiology.

quiz.q: Which oxygen target is correct for a patient with known COPD?
choices: 100% at all times
quiz.why: COPD patients are titrated to 88 to 92% rather than the 94 to 99% target used for most patients. Driving saturation to 100% is not a goal in any patient, and 80 to 85% is hypoxia, not a target.

quiz.q: A 2-year-old has a barking cough that started at night, mild inspiratory stridor, a low fever, and no drooling. She is alert and will drink. The most likely condition and management are:
choices: Epiglottitis; keep her calm and do not inspect the throat
Croup; keep her calm, allow a position of comfort, humidified air and oxygen as tolerated, and transport
Anaphylaxis; give epinephrine 0.15 mg intramuscular
Foreign body airway obstruction; begin back blows and chest thrusts
quiz.why: A barking cough worse at night in a toddler with a low fever and no drooling is croup, a viral illness managed with calm, humidity and transport. Epiglottitis brings drooling, tripod posture, a high fever and no cough, anaphylaxis needs an exposure and hives or hypotension, and a child who can cough and drink is not obstructed.

quiz.q: A 68-year-old in pulmonary edema is on CPAP at 8 cmH2O. He initially improved. Now he is vomiting into the mask and his systolic has dropped from 156 to 84. You should:
choices: Increase CPAP to 12 cmH2O to overcome the fluid
Leave CPAP in place and suction around the mask
Remove CPAP, clear the airway with suction, and assist ventilations with a bag-valve mask
Remove CPAP and place a nasal cannula at 6 L/min
quiz.why: Vomiting and a falling blood pressure are both reasons to stop CPAP, since positive pressure reduces venous return and a mask over a vomiting airway invites aspiration. The patient now needs a cleared airway and assisted ventilation, not more pressure and not a low-flow device.

quiz.q: During a two-rescuer adult resuscitation you notice frequent pauses for pulse checks and equipment. What quality target is most directly threatened?
choices: Compression depth of 2 to 2.4 inches
A compression rate of 100 to 120 per minute
Full chest recoil between compressions
A compression fraction above 60% with interruptions under 10 seconds
quiz.why: Repeated pauses attack hands-off time, which is measured as compression fraction and the 10-second interruption limit. Depth, rate and recoil are qualities of the compressions actually delivered, not of the gaps between them.

quiz.q: A 58-year-old regains a pulse after defibrillation. He is unresponsive with a blood pressure of 104/62 and an SpO2 of 96%. Your partner begins bagging him at 24 breaths per minute. You should:
choices: Slow ventilation to about 10 breaths per minute, targeting an ETCO2 of 35 to 45 and a saturation of 92 to 98%
Continue at 24 breaths per minute to wash out acid
Stop ventilating entirely and apply a nonrebreather
Resume compressions because the pressure is low
quiz.why: Post-arrest hyperventilation is the most commonly tested error: it raises intrathoracic pressure, drops venous return and lowers cerebral blood flow. Ten breaths a minute to an ETCO2 of 35 to 45 is the target, and a patient with a pulse and a systolic above 90 does not get compressions.

quiz.q: A 40-year-old stabbed in the left chest has a blood pressure of 78/62, distended neck veins, muffled heart tones, and equal breath sounds bilaterally. The most likely problem is:
choices: Tension pneumothorax
Cardiac tamponade
Hypovolemic shock from blood loss
Massive pulmonary embolism
quiz.why: Muffled tones, distended neck veins and a narrowing pulse pressure with equal breath sounds are the tamponade picture. Tension pneumothorax would give absent breath sounds on one side, and hypovolemia produces flat neck veins rather than distended ones.

quiz.q: Which rhythms will an AED shock?
choices: Asystole and pulseless electrical activity
Any rhythm faster than 150
Ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Atrial fibrillation with a pulse
quiz.why: Only ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia are shockable. Asystole and PEA are not, a rate alone does not determine shockability, and a patient with a pulse is never defibrillated by an AED.

quiz.q: A 62-year-old two weeks after knee surgery has sudden severe shortness of breath, clear lung sounds, a heart rate of 124, and an SpO2 that stays at 87% on a nonrebreather at 15 L/min. The most likely cause is:
choices: Acute pulmonary edema from left-sided heart failure
An asthma exacerbation
Pneumonia
A massive pulmonary embolism
quiz.why: Sudden dyspnea with clear lungs and hypoxia that does not respond to high-flow oxygen after recent surgery and immobility is the classic PE pattern. Pulmonary edema gives crackles, asthma gives wheezes, and pneumonia develops over days with fever and focal findings.

quiz.q: A head-injured 30-year-old opens his eyes to pain, makes incomprehensible sounds, and withdraws from pain. His Glasgow Coma Scale total and its main implication are:
choices: 8, a patient who cannot reliably protect his own airway
10, a patient who can protect his airway
6, requiring immediate defibrillation
12, requiring only observation
quiz.why: Eye opening to pain is 2, incomprehensible sounds is 2, and withdrawal from pain is 4, totaling 8. A GCS of 8 or less marks a patient who cannot protect an airway, which drives airway management and destination, not observation.

quiz.q: A 50-year-old thrown from a motorcycle has an unstable pelvis, a heart rate of 132, and a blood pressure of 84/58. Correct field management includes:
choices: Repeated pelvic compression to monitor for changes
A pelvic binder or sheet applied at the level of the greater trochanters, with rapid transport
Log-rolling the patient repeatedly to inspect the back
A traction splint applied to both legs
quiz.why: A binder at the greater trochanters closes the pelvic ring and limits massive internal bleeding. Repeated compression and unnecessary rolling disrupt clot and worsen bleeding, and traction splints are for mid-shaft femur fractures, not pelvic instability.

quiz.q: A trauma patient bleeding from multiple sites has been fully exposed for assessment in a 15 C ambulance compartment. Which statement best explains why this matters?
choices: Cooling reduces metabolic demand and is protective in trauma
Temperature only matters in burn patients
Hypothermia impairs clotting and is one leg of the trauma triad of death along with acidosis and coagulopathy
Exposure is irrelevant once bleeding is controlled with dressings
quiz.why: Cold blood does not clot well, so hypothermia directly worsens hemorrhage and feeds the acidosis and coagulopathy of the trauma triad. Exposure is necessary for assessment, but leaving the patient uncovered afterward is an active harm rather than a neutral act.

quiz.q: A 24-year-old has been seizing continuously for about 8 minutes with no return to consciousness. Correct management includes:
choices: Restraining the limbs to prevent injury
Placing a bite block between the teeth
Withholding oxygen until the seizure stops
Protecting him from injury, managing the airway, checking a glucose, and requesting ALS for status epilepticus
quiz.why: Continuous seizing beyond 5 minutes is status epilepticus and needs ALS for a benzodiazepine. You protect without restraining, never place anything in the mouth, and oxygen is given during the seizure rather than withheld.

quiz.q: A 71-year-old with left-sided weakness was last known well 2 hours ago. Which action is most important?
choices: Establish and report the last known well time and transport to a stroke center with early notification
Give aspirin 324 mg chewed
Apply a nonrebreather at 15 L/min regardless of saturation
Delay transport to repeat the stroke scale three times
quiz.why: Time decides what the hospital can offer: clot-dissolving drugs are generally considered within 3 to 4.5 hours of last known well. Aspirin is never given for stroke because the bleed cannot be excluded in the field, oxygen is titrated rather than automatic, and repeating the scale wastes the window.

quiz.q: Which assessment should be performed on every patient with altered mental status?
choices: A 12-lead ECG
A blood glucose measurement
A pelvic compression
An oral temperature
quiz.why: Hypoglycemia is a rapidly reversible cause of altered mental status and sits in the middle of the AEIOU-TIPS list, so glucose is checked on every altered patient. The other assessments are situational and none of them catches a treatable cause this quickly.

quiz.q: A farm worker is found beside a spilled pesticide container with pinpoint pupils, drooling, vomiting, urinary incontinence and copious secretions. Your first action is:
choices: Suction the airway and begin ventilation immediately
Move him into the ambulance and start oxygen
Decontaminate, removing clothing and washing the skin, before treatment and transport
Give naloxone for the pinpoint pupils
quiz.why: These SLUDGEM findings point to organophosphate poisoning, and the chemical remains on his skin and clothing, contaminating you and the ambulance. Decontamination comes before treatment; naloxone treats opioids, which do not cause this pattern of secretions.

quiz.q: A 26-year-old woman has right lower quadrant pain that began around the navel, a low-grade fever, and nausea. Her last menstrual period was two weeks ago and a home pregnancy test yesterday was negative. She has no syncope and a blood pressure of 118/72. The most likely cause is:
choices: Ectopic pregnancy, which must be assumed in any woman of childbearing age
Aortic dissection
Ovarian torsion, which never causes fever
Appendicitis, suggested by periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant
quiz.why: Pain that starts periumbilical and migrates to the right lower quadrant with fever and nausea is the classic appendicitis pattern. Ectopic pregnancy remains on the list for any woman of childbearing age, but a recent normal period, a negative test and stable vitals without syncope make appendicitis far more likely, and dissection presents as tearing pain to the back with unequal arm pressures.

quiz.q: Under the incident command system, span of control means one supervisor should directly manage how many people?
choices: 3 to 7, ideally 5
1 to 2
8 to 10
Unlimited, as long as radios work
quiz.why: Span of control runs 3 to 7 subordinates with 5 as the target. Fewer wastes supervisors at a large incident, and more than 7 means a supervisor loses track of assignments and accountability.

quiz.q: You arrive at a overturned tanker leaking an unknown liquid with a placard you cannot read from the road. Correct positioning is:
choices: Downwind so the plume blows away from the patients
Upwind, uphill and upstream, at least 100 feet from the hazard, reading the placard with binoculars
Directly beside the tanker so you can reach the driver quickly
Downhill so runoff moves away from the ambulance
quiz.why: Upwind, uphill and upstream keeps vapor, runoff and liquid away from you, with at least 100 feet of standoff and a 2,000 foot isolation zone for a suspected large spill until the Emergency Response Guidebook says otherwise. Downwind and downhill both put you in the path of the product, and approaching the tanker enters an unsafe scene.

quiz.q: You transmit a radio report and medical control orders a medication. What must you do before administering it?
choices: Ask your partner to confirm the order
Document the order and administer it, then confirm on arrival
Repeat the order back word for word
Request the order in writing from the hospital
quiz.why: Echoing the order back word for word is how a misheard drug, dose or route gets caught before it reaches the patient. Confirming with a partner, documenting later, or waiting for written orders all skip the one check that happens in real time.

quiz.q: A police officer offers to run ahead of your ambulance as an escort through heavy traffic to shorten transport by several minutes. You should:
choices: Accept, since police escorts are the fastest safe option
Accept but disable your siren so drivers hear only one
Accept if the patient is unstable and decline if stable
Decline, because drivers who yield to the first vehicle often pull out into the second
quiz.why: Escorts and convoy driving are avoided because motorists who stopped for the lead vehicle assume the emergency has passed and pull back out in front of the ambulance. Patient acuity does not change the physics, and turning off your siren removes a warning rather than adding one.

quiz.q: A stem describes an asthma patient who was wheezing and diaphoretic, states that after assisted ventilation and albuterol he is now alert with easier breathing and a saturation of 96%, then asks what you should do. The pattern and the answer are:
choices: Improvement after treatment; reassess and continue care rather than escalating
Deterioration after an intervention; reverse what you did
Two correct actions; the cue word decides the order
Scene hazard buried mid-stem; address safety first
quiz.why: When the stem tells you the patient improved, the answer is to reassess and continue, not to add an intervention. Candidates routinely confuse this with the mirror pattern, where a patient worsens right after something you did and the answer points back at that intervention.

quiz.q: A 55-year-old with crushing chest pain and a systolic of 140 has no nitroglycerin of his own, but his wife offers hers. What does this stem shape tell you?
choices: Assist with her nitroglycerin, since the indication and blood pressure both fit
This is the 'medication belongs to someone else' pattern, so you never assist with a drug not prescribed to this patient
Contact medical control to authorize use of a family member's prescription
Assist only if the wife's dose is 0.4 mg
quiz.why: EMT scope covers assisting a patient with medication prescribed to that patient. A perfect indication and an acceptable pressure are the bait; the prescription label is the disqualifier, and dose matching does not change that.

quiz.q: You are running the trauma assessment station. After the primary survey and your transport decision, what is the correct next scored component?
choices: OPQRST history of the pain
Full baseline vital signs before touching the patient again
A rapid head-to-toe trauma exam using DCAP-BTLS
A focused exam of only the obviously injured limb
quiz.why: The trauma station moves from the primary survey and transport decision into a rapid head-to-toe exam narrated with DCAP-BTLS, with vitals and SAMPLE following. OPQRST drives the medical station, and examining only the obvious injury misses the ones that kill.

quiz.q: A candidate performs a full head-to-toe rapid trauma exam on a medical station patient with shortness of breath, then runs out of time before taking a history. What went wrong?
choices: Nothing; a thorough exam always scores well
He should have skipped the primary survey to save time
He should have taken vitals first in both stations
He applied the trauma station's shape to a medical patient, where history drives the assessment and the exam is focused
quiz.why: In the trauma station you find injuries with a head-to-toe sweep; in the medical station you build a story with OPQRST and SAMPLE, then focus the exam on the system the history points at. Mixing the two costs the scored history components, and the primary survey is never skipped.

quiz.q: You notice you are spending about 100 seconds per item and rereading each stem twice. The best adjustment is:
choices: Read the stem once, reread only the last line for the cue word, then decide and move on
Read each stem three times to be certain
Skip the difficult items and return to them at the end
Guess randomly on the remaining items to save time
quiz.why: The target is 45 to 60 seconds per item, and consistently exceeding 90 seconds means rereading rather than deciding. Returning to items is impossible on an adaptive exam, and random guessing throws away information you actually have.

quiz.q: Two weeks before the exam a candidate is highly anxious. Which approach most reliably lowers that anxiety?
choices: Rereading the textbook chapters he finds most reassuring
Sitting two or three full-length 120-question sessions under real conditions, timed, with no phone, notes or pausing
Telling himself repeatedly that he is prepared
Increasing caffeine on exam day to raise alertness
quiz.why: Simulation lowers arousal by making the unfamiliar familiar, which reassurance alone cannot do. Rereading builds false confidence without retrieval practice, and an unusual caffeine load on exam day tests an unknown physiologic response on the one day it matters.
